```python
def test_select_words():
    # Basic examples
    assert select_words("Mary had a little lamb", 4) == ["little"]
    assert select_words("Mary had a little lamb", 3) == ["Mary", "lamb"]
    assert select_words("simple white space", 2) == []
    assert select_words("Hello world", 4) == ["world"]

    # Case insensitivity of vowel check
    assert select_words("APPLE pear Plum", 3) == ["APPLE", "pear", "Plum"]

    # Zero consonants: only words made entirely of vowels
    assert select_words("a e i o u ae io", 0) == ["a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "ae", "io"]

    # Empty string returns empty list
    assert select_words("", 3) == []

    # No word matches the required consonant count
    assert select_words("cat dog bird", 10) == []

    # Single word strings
    assert select_words("world", 4) == ["world"]
    assert select_words("hello", 3) == ["hello"]

    # 'y' is treated as a consonant (not in the vowel list)
    assert select_words("rhythm why", 6) == ["rhythm"]
    assert select_words("yay", 2) == ["yay"]

    # Words with duplicate letters counted correctly
    assert select_words("aa bb ccc", 2) == ["bb"]

    # Multiple spaces between words are handled by split()
    assert select_words("Mary   had   a   little   lamb", 3) == ["Mary", "lamb"]

    # All words match
    assert select_words("dog cat", 2) == ["dog", "cat"]
```
